title: Guided tour
replayDesc: Walk through the dashboard basics again.

pages.title: Your pages
pages.body: Each tab is a separate page. Add as many as you need — one per room, one per floor, whatever fits.

edit.title: Edit mode
edit.body: The pencil unlocks the grid: drag, resize, configure or delete your widgets. Nothing moves until you turn it on.

add.title: Add a widget
add.body: Open the catalogue and pick a card: light, camera, sensor, thermostat… then choose the entity it controls.

addPage.title: A new page
addPage.body: Add a page to split your dashboard by room or by floor. Each page keeps its own grid.

save.title: Save
save.body: Nothing is persisted until you save. Cancel with the cross to drop every change made since entering edit mode.

dock.title: The dock
dock.body: The bottom bar opens your panels. Its gear icon lets you reorder them or add new ones.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Theme, layout, language, backup. Everything that changes the look of the dashboard lives here.

widgetsAdd.title: The catalogue
widgetsAdd.body: Widgets are grouped by category. Pick one, then select the Home Assistant entity it should control.

widgetsResize.title: Arrange the grid
widgetsResize.body: In edit mode each card can be dragged, and resized from its bottom-right corner. Each screen size keeps its own layout.

widgetsSave.title: Keep your work
widgetsSave.body: Save once the layout suits you. Your dashboard is stored on the server, so every device sees it.

panelsCreate.title: Custom panels
panelsCreate.body: A panel is a full-screen sheet you build from blocks: cover rows, action buttons, section titles.

panelsDock.title: Put it in the dock
panelsDock.body: Once a panel exists, add it to the bottom bar from the gear icon — it becomes one tap away.

panelsSave.title: Save
panelsSave.body: Panels are saved along with the rest of the dashboard.

appearanceOpen.title: Themes
appearanceOpen.body: Seven themes, card opacity, wallpaper, automatic day/night switching — all in the appearance section.

appearanceWallpanel.title: Wall panel mode
appearanceWallpanel.body: Set up a screensaver layout for a tablet mounted on the wall: it takes over after a while idle.
